australian-magpie.name: Australian Magpie
australian-magpie.description: A medium-sized black and white songbird famous for its beautiful caroling and remarkable intelligence.

images.author: jg001
images.caption: Taken August 8, 2022 in Encounter Bay, South Australia.

images.author: jg001
images.caption: Taken August 8, 2022 in Encounter Bay, South Australia.

facts.title: Awesome Imitator
facts.description: Magpies can mimic car alarms, barking dogs, and even human speech - they're nature's feathered sound machines!

facts.title: Melodic Master
facts.description: They sing over 300 different songs, some so complex they take a year for young magpies to learn properly.

facts.title: Never Forget a Face
facts.description: These clever birds recognize individual humans and remember who's been kind or mean to them for years.

facts.title: Backyard Explorer
facts.description: From city parks to remote forests, magpies thrive everywhere in Australia - even doing 'turf inspections' on football fields!

facts.title: Omnivore Adventure
facts.description: They hunt like ninjas - stalking insects with beak probes, snatching lizards mid-sprint, and even stealing picnic snacks!

black-faced-cuckooshrike.name: Black-faced Cuckooshrike
black-faced-cuckooshrike.description: A sleek grey bird with a mysterious black mask, famous for its smooth gliding flights.

facts.title: Hybrid Appearance
facts.description: Named for its mix of cuckoo-like wings and shrike-like beak - nature's perfect combo!

facts.title: Urban Glider
facts.description: Watch them surfing city air currents - they perform graceful aerial dances between skyscrapers and trees.

facts.title: Bug Buffet
facts.description: They specialize in caterpillar feasts, shaking hairy insects violently to remove prickly bits before eating.

facts.title: Feathered Meteor
facts.description: When flying between trees, they tuck wings close and drop like grey rockets before swooping up at the last second!

facts.title: Secret Singer
facts.description: Listen for their soft 'churring' love songs during breeding season - like tiny marbles rolling in a cup.

crimson-rosella.name: Crimson Rosella
crimson-rosella.description: A brilliantly colored parrot that looks like a flying rainbow against green forests.

facts.title: Colour Changers
facts.description: Babies wear green camouflage jackets before transforming into dazzling red-and-blue adults - nature's glow-up!

facts.title: Mountain Acrobat
facts.description: They perform daring aerial rolls while chasing mates through snowy eucalyptus forests.

facts.title: Seed Crusher
facts.description: Special beak grooves let them perfectly crack hard nuts while hanging upside down like feathered monkeys!

facts.title: Whistle Wizard
facts.description: Some learn human tunes and can whistle entire songs back to people who teach them.

facts.title: Family Party
facts.description: Youngsters stay with parents for a year, forming colorful feeding flocks that chatter like excited kids at a playground.

flame-robin.name: Flame Robin
flame-robin.description: A small bird with a fiery orange chest that looks like a living ember hopping through the undergrowth.

facts.title: Mountain Nomad
facts.description: They summer in snowy highlands then migrate to valleys - tiny mountaineers with feathery snow boots!

facts.title: Love Glow
facts.description: Males' chests turn brighter orange when seeking mates - like putting on a neon 'date me' sign!

facts.title: Ground Sniper
facts.description: They perch low, then drop silently onto unsuspecting insects - pouncing with ninja-like precision.

facts.title: Dawn Serenader
facts.description: Males sing sweet melodies from fence posts at sunrise - nature's alarm clock with feathers.

facts.title: Flash and Hide
facts.description: When predators approach, they flash white tail feathers as distraction signals before vanishing.

gang-gang-cockatoo.name: Gang-gang Cockatoo
gang-gang-cockatoo.description: A quirky grey cockatoo where males sport punk-rock red heads and make sounds like creaky doors.

facts.title: ACT Superstar
facts.description: Official bird emblem of Australia's capital - they're feathered celebrities in Canberra!

facts.title: Squeaky Toy
facts.description: Their call sounds exactly like a rusty gate - nature's comedy sound effect artists!

facts.title: Berry Lover
facts.description: They twist berries off stems with foot-beak teamwork while hanging like acrobatic fruit bats.

facts.title: Alpine Adventurer
facts.description: One of few parrots that thrives in snowy mountains - wearing fluffy feather coats against the cold.

facts.title: Treehouse Family
facts.description: They return to the exact same tree hollow for decades, passing 'family homes' through generations.

galah.name: Galah
galah.description: A pink-and-grey acrobat often seen doing playful mid-air somersaults in huge chattering flocks.

facts.title: Sky Dancer
facts.description: They celebrate rain with aerial cartwheels - tumbling through air like feathered gymnasts!

facts.title: Bulldozer Beak
facts.description: They dig up roots with powerful beaks while standing on one foot - like pink feathered excavators.

facts.title: City Slicker
facts.description: They've mastered traffic patterns, safely crossing roads by hopping between cars at red lights!

facts.title: Silly Billy
facts.description: Australians call foolish people 'galahs' because these birds do hilarious things like hanging upside down just for fun!

facts.title: Lovebirds
facts.description: Partners preen each other daily and share food - they even blush pinker when reunited after separations!

laughing-kookaburra.name: Laughing Kookaburra
laughing-kookaburra.description: A stout kingfisher with a legendary laugh that sounds like a rollicking jungle chorus.

facts.title: Breakfast Alarm
facts.description: Families 'laugh' together at dawn - the original Australian wake-up call for miles around!

facts.title: Snake Hunter
facts.description: They grab venomous snakes behind the head and bash them against branches - feathered warriors!

facts.title: Movie Star
facts.description: Their laugh features in jungle films worldwide - even in Africa where they don't live!

facts.title: Territory Boss
facts.description: Families defend territories for generations with special laughs that say: 'This is OUR land!'

facts.title: Patient Fisher
facts.description: They perch motionless for hours, then dive like feathered torpedoes to snatch fish from streams.

noisy-friarbird.name: Noisy Friarbird
noisy-friarbird.description: A bald-headed honeyeater that sounds like a cackling witch when chasing rivals through treetops.

facts.title: Bald Power
facts.description: Their bare black head prevents sticky nectar from gluing feathers - nature's ingenious kitchen hack!

facts.title: Noise Champion
facts.description: Their raucous 'cackle-gargle' calls carry over 500m - the loudest song in the honeyeater family!

facts.title: Flower Bandit
facts.description: They pierce flower bases to 'steal' nectar without pollinating - garden thieves in feathers!

facts.title: Feather Gang
facts.description: They lead mixed bird flocks through forests, shouting orders like feathery drill sergeants.

facts.title: Fruit Fighter
facts.description: They battle possums for figs at night, cackling furiously while wrestling for juicy prizes!

pied-currawong.name: Pied Currawong
pied-currawong.description: A bold black-and-white songster with haunting flute-like calls echoing through misty forests.

facts.title: Mystery Musician
facts.description: Their beautiful 'curra-wong' calls sound like wooden flutes playing in hidden mountain valleys.

facts.title: Egg Hunter
facts.description: They sneak into nests when parents are away, swallowing eggs whole like feathery pirates!

facts.title: Winter Wanderers
facts.description: In cold months, they form huge flocks that descend on towns like feathered snowstorms.

facts.title: Fruit Lover
facts.description: They gorge on berries until drunk, then wobble on branches singing slurred songs!

facts.title: Nature's Cleaner
facts.description: They clean roads by eating roadkill insects - feathered street sweepers with beautiful voices!

rainbow-lorikeet.name: Rainbow Lorikeet
rainbow-lorikeet.description: A living kaleidoscope that flashes through trees in noisy, quarrelsome flocks.

facts.title: Nectar Toothbrush
facts.description: Their tongue has tiny brushes on the tip that soak up nectar like a feathery drinking straw!

facts.title: Color Splash
facts.description: Their rainbow feathers aren't just pretty - they blend perfectly with colorful flowers while feeding!

facts.title: Fruit Vandals
facts.description: They ravage orchards, piercing hundreds of fruits daily just for tiny sips - messy eaters!

facts.title: Apartment Nester
facts.description: In cities, they nest inside building walls - squawky tenants who never pay rent!

facts.title: Play Fighters
facts.description: They hang upside down to wrestle friends with soft beak nibbles - like feathery MMA fighters!

red-wattlebird.name: Red Wattlebird
red-wattlebird.description: A large, bossy honeyeater with red face wattles that dangle like quirky earrings.

facts.title: Wiggle Wattles
facts.description: They shake red face wattles during courtship dances - like feathered hula dancers!

facts.title: Nectar Robber
facts.description: They pierce flower bases to steal nectar without pollinating - garden rebels with wattles!

facts.title: Noisy Neighbor
facts.description: Their 'cookay-cok' calls sound like squeaky pumps - nature's alarm system at dawn!

facts.title: Berry Gobbler
facts.description: They swallow whole berries then later cough up seeds - helping forests grow new trees!

facts.title: Feather Bodyguard
facts.description: They aggressively chase hawks away from gardens - tiny but fierce protectors!

spotted-pardalote.name: Spotted Pardalote
spotted-pardalote.description: Australia's tiniest gem - a jeweled bird smaller than a mouse with starry spots on its wings.

facts.title: Flying Diamonds
facts.description: Their wings sparkle with white spots like starry constellations against forest shadows.

facts.title: Tunnel Engineer
facts.description: They dig 1m long tunnels in riverbanks for nests - tiny feathered miners with pick-axe beaks!

facts.title: Treetop Diner
facts.description: They only eat while hanging upside down under leaves - nature's acrobatic snackers!

facts.title: Secret Song
facts.description: Their soft 'sleep-may-beetle' song sounds like a sleepy child whispering secrets.

facts.title: Speedy Flicker
facts.description: They move so fast through treetops, they look like flashing Christmas lights in the canopy!

superb-fairywren.name: Superb Fairywren
superb-fairywren.description: A tiny electric-blue dancer that pops against green grass like a living sapphire.

facts.title: Costume Change
facts.description: Males transform from brown to brilliant blue for dating season - nature's quick-change artists!

facts.title: Secret Admirers
facts.description: Females sneak off to meet 'boyfriend' wrens while their main partner guards the nest!

facts.title: Grasshopper Alarm
facts.description: They make special 'trill' calls to warn friends about predators - feathery security guards!

facts.title: Spiderweb Fashion
facts.description: They decorate nests with spiderwebs and flower petals - feathered interior designers!

facts.title: Follow the Leader
facts.description: They hop behind kangaroos catching insects stirred up by their feet - clever hitchhikers!

sulphur-crested-cockatoo.name: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo
sulphur-crested-cockatoo.description: A bold white parrot with a sunshine-yellow crown that loves showing off with ear-splitting screeches.

facts.title: Crest Communicator
facts.description: They raise their yellow crown when excited - like feathered mood rings showing their feelings!

facts.title: Bin Bandits
facts.description: In cities, they teach each other to open trash bins - feathery hackers in broad daylight!

facts.title: Wood Chewer
facts.description: Their super-strong beaks can demolish wooden decks - nature's feathery chainsaws!

facts.title: Dance Party
facts.description: They bob heads and spread wings in synchronized group dances - feathered flash mob performers!

facts.title: Lifelong Friends
facts.description: They live 70+ years, recognizing human friends decades later with excited squawks!

tawny-frogmouth.name: Tawny Frogmouth
tawny-frogmouth.description: A master of disguise that freezes like a broken branch, with huge frog-like eyes for night hunting.

facts.title: Hide and Seek Champ
facts.description: They point beaks upward and close eyes to slits - becoming near-invisible tree extensions!

facts.title: Bug Zapper
facts.description: They catch moths mid-air with their huge beaks - nature's silent night-time vacuum cleaners!

facts.title: Not an Owl!
facts.description: Despite appearances, they're related to nightjars and catch prey with beaks, not talons.

facts.title: Love Sticks
facts.description: Mates groom each other with special 'love sticks' they find and present as gifts!

facts.title: Tree Hugger
facts.description: Chicks hug branches with wings spread flat - looking like adorable feathery pancakes!

welcome-swallow.name: Welcome Swallow
welcome-swallow.description: A speedy blue acrobat with forked tail streamers that twist through air like feathered fighter jets.

facts.title: Mud Architect
facts.description: They build nests from 1,000+ mud pellets - tiny feathered bricklayers crafting cozy homes!

facts.title: Wind Rider
facts.description: They fly 35 km/h while making sharp 90-degree turns to catch insects mid-air!

facts.title: Barn Buddy
facts.description: They nest inside barns and sheds, eating flies that bother livestock - farmers' feathery friends!

facts.title: Ocean Crosser
facts.description: Some migrate 2,500km from Tasmania to New Guinea - tiny birds crossing vast oceans!

facts.title: Dust Bather
facts.description: They flutter in dirt roads to clean feathers - taking happy dust baths like feathered spa lovers!

white-throated-treecreeper.name: White-throated Treecreeper
white-throated-treecreeper.description: A tree-trunk detective that spirals upward while probing bark crevices with its curved beak.

facts.title: Bark Inspector
facts.description: They only climb upward on trees, hopping down to restart - nature's feathered spiral stair climbers!

facts.title: Tail Prop
facts.description: Stiff tail feathers act as kickstands against tree trunks - built-in climbing gear!

facts.title: Forest Doctor
facts.description: They eat harmful tree-boring insects - feathered forest medics saving sick trees!

facts.title: Secret Whistler
facts.description: Mates sing soft duets while climbing together - like whispering sweet nothings up tree trunks!

facts.title: Cavity Sleeper
facts.description: They sleep jammed into narrow bark crevices - cozy feathery wedges in nature's tree pockets!

willie-wagtail.name: Willie Wagtail
willie-wagtail.description: A feisty little dancer with a constantly wiggling tail that chases away birds 10 times its size!

facts.title: Tail Talker
facts.description: They wag tails side-to-side to scare insects into moving - like feathery fishing lures!

facts.title: Fearless Fighter
facts.description: They dive-bomb eagles and kookaburras - tiny ninjas protecting their turf!

facts.title: Campfire Friend
facts.description: They follow campers to catch insects stirred by footsteps - nature's cleanup crew!

facts.title: Mirror Warrior
facts.description: They attack car mirrors, thinking reflections are rivals - feathered knights jousting with reflections!

facts.title: Moonlight Singer
facts.description: On bright nights, they sing sweet songs from rooftops - feathery midnight troubadours!
